record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: For every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, is the symmetric separation constant K_s(X) strictly greater than 1? Here K_s(X) is the supremum of all sigma > 0 for which there exists a sequence (x_n) in the unit ball B_X such that ||x_n + x_m|| >= sigma and ||x_n - x_m|| >= sigma whenever n != m.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space with closed unit ball B_X. Define the symmetric separation constant K_s(X) to be the supremum of all σ > 0 for which there exists a sequence (x_n) in B_X such that, for all n ≠ m,
  ‖x_n + x_m‖ ≥ σ  and  ‖x_n − x_m‖ ≥ σ.
Prove or disprove: for every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, one has K_s(X) > 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively. T. Kania (and related work by Hájek–Kania–Russo) proved that K^s(X) > 1 for every infinite-dimensional Banach space, establishing a symmetric version of the Elton–Odell theorem and resolving the question posed by Castillo and Papini.

status_evidence.title: A note on symmetric separation in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: We show that K^s(X)>1, for every infinite-dimensional Banach space, thereby solving a problem by J.M.F. Castillo and P.L. Papini.
status_evidence.claim: Proves K_s(X) > 1 for every infinite-dimensional Banach space, solving the problem.

status_evidence.title: Symmetrically separated sequences in the unit sphere of a Banach space
status_evidence.snippet: Symmetrically (1+epsilon)-separated sequences in unit sphere of infinite-dimensional Banach spaces.
